facts.fact: The Births and Deaths Registration Act, as consolidated to 6 March 2020, requires the registrar of each district to keep registers in the prescribed form and to sign and forward every notice of birth, still-birth or death and every medical certificate of cause of death to the Registrar-General by registered post, the Registrar-General keeping registers of his own (sections 3 to 5); the text as captured makes no provision for an electronic register or record.

The Births and Deaths Registration Act, as consolidated to 6 March 2020, assigns its administration to the Minister of Home Affairs and establishes a Registrar-General of Births and Deaths as the central registering office, with a registrar for each district (sections 2 and 3).

systems.platform: registers in the prescribed form; notices forwarded by registered post
systems.owner: Registrar-General of Births and Deaths, under the Minister of Home Affairs
systems.tiers: a registrar for each district, with deputy and assistant registrars; the Registrar-General's office as the central registering office

note: The captured text stops mid-sentence in section 27(3)(b), so the end of the Act was not read. The made value rests on the statute's registers and registered post, not on a statement that offices use paper today. Notice of a birth is due within 42 days, of a death within 30.
